title: Endpoint latency skyline comparator: streaming vs non-streaming
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Build a comparative latency dashboard that surfaces p50/p95/p99 and request-rate for every model + route combination with a split between streaming and non-streaming I/O modes. This ticket covers the backend aggregation logic, trace hook alignment, UX wireframe, and dashboard panels for SREs and product engineers to quickly identify regressions that only appear in streaming or non-streaming paths.
background: We currently have percentile metrics but they are noisy when mixing streaming and non-streaming requests. Streaming requests have different serving paths (partial token emission, longer-lived connections) so percentiles aggregated together mask regressions that affect only one I/O mode. Several recent incidents flagged higher p95 in streaming routes that were invisible in the global endpoint dashboard.
goals: Expose p50/p95/p99 and qps broken down by model + route + io_mode (stream | non-stream)
Make latency time-series and percentile histograms queryable for arbitrary windows (1m/5m/1h/24h)
Add trace links from any percentile spike to the correlated trace slices (Tempo/Jaeger) and relevant logs
Keep dashboard queries inexpensive by leveraging pre-aggregated histograms or summary tables
acceptance_criteria: New dashboard with separate panels showing streaming and non-streaming percentiles for selected model and route
Percentile panels support hover-to-see sample count and auto-link to traces for that percentile window
Backend aggregates do not increase query cost by more than 30% compared to current endpoint panels under normal load
Unit and integration tests for aggregation logic and trace hook correlation
Design review completed and UX approved by @Maya Patel
tasks: Design: final wireframe for skyline comparator and percentile breakdowns (DES-2204)
Backend: add io_mode tag to telemetry ingestion pipeline and update histogram rollups
Query infra: implement pre-aggregated histogram tables in ClickHouse and a fallback live-aggregation path
Tracing: extend trace hooks to tag spans with route + model + io_mode and ensure sampling is correlated
Dashboard: build panel in Console with model/route selector, streaming toggle, and trace links
Docs: update runbook and dashboard playbook with investigation steps for stream/non-stream regressions
Performance: validate query latency under synthetic QPS and tune retention/partitioning
notes: We will use HDR histograms for percentile accuracy and store compressed summaries in ClickHouse summary tables.
io_mode detection: streaming if request uses chunked response or websocket/grpc streaming, otherwise non-streaming.
Trace linking: start by adding a trace_id field in percentile samples when sample_count > threshold (100) to bias toward high-volume windows.
Fallback plan: if adding io_mode tag to ingestion causes a spike in cardinality, enable a sampled ingestion path that populates the comparator only for top-100 routes per model.
Related tickets: ENG-82455 (streaming trace hooks), ENG-701234 (histogram rollups)
Design owner: Maya Patel; SRE reviewer: Omar Hassan; Product reviewer: Nina Sato
implementation_details: Telemetry ingestion: extend OTLP collector to attach 'io_mode' attribute and forward to metrics pipeline
Aggregation: nightly job to populate summary histograms for 1m/5m buckets; real-time 1m window served by materialized views
Query layer: new SQL macro percentile_by_io(model, route, io_mode, p) that reads pre-agg if available else computes from raw histograms
Trace hooks: Instrument serving runtime to emit span tags: model.name, route.path, io_mode, request.shape; ensure sampling key is model+route
Dashboard: React + Vega-lite panel with two overlaid percentile lines (stream vs non-stream) and a stacked QPS bar below
risks_and_mitigation: Cardinality explosion from model+route+io_mode: mitigate with sampling and top-k focus; monitor ClickHouse storage and set retention policies
False correlation between percentile spikes and traces: require a minimum sample count and use probabilistic linking heuristics
Query cost regression: use pre-aggregates and limit time range selectors by default

Omar (SRE): require alert thresholds for diverging stream vs non-stream p95 by >30% for a sustained 10m window
Nina (Product): add example investigation steps linking to common failure modes (kv-cache miss, kernel fallback)
qa_plan: Unit tests for histogram rollup functions

Accuracy test: compare percentiles computed from pre-agg vs raw histograms for random model-route pairs
